## What the data says
- All eight nearest thin-fabric test runs at 20.7-21.6 % O₂ and 101.3 kPa sustained burning; distance-weighted share = 100 % [PSI-25] [PSI-98]
- Evidence coverage for thin fabric at Earth-sea-level conditions is 0.986 (8 runs) [PSI-25] [PSI-98]
- Physics estimate (n-heptane surrogate) places the adiabatic flame temperature (~2270 K) 50 K below the hottest thin-fabric microgravity run (~2320 K) and 260 K above the coldest burning run (~2010 K) [PSI-25] [PSI-98]
- Thin solid (films, sheets) had 7 sustained and 1 marginal out of 8 runs at 21 % O₂, 101.3 kPa; distance-weighted share = 93.8 % [PSI-25]
- Evidence coverage for thin solid is 1.0 (8 runs) [PSI-25]
- Physics estimate for thin solid places the adiabatic flame temperature (~2270 K) 50 K below the hottest thin-solid run (~2330 K) and 360 K above the coldest burning run (~1910 K) [PSI-25]
- Droplet tests with methanol at 21 % O₂, 101-101.9 kPa, 0 cm/s flow: all 8 runs sustained burning; physics margin ≈ 550 K above limiting flame temperature (~1670 K) (FLEX calibration) [PSI-69]
- Droplet tests with n-heptane at the same conditions: all 8 runs sustained; physics margin ≈ 360 K above limiting flame temperature (~1860 K) [PSI-69]
- Fire-resistant materials: 3 of 4 Nomex runs burned, 1 did not; 0 of 4 silicone runs burned (5 of 8 runs did not sustain) [PSI-25] [PSI-99]
- Nomex failed NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 at 30 % O₂, 70.1 kPa in 1 g (NASA report) (NTRS 20070018178)
- Partial-gravity combustion is untested; lunar-gravity may lower the oxygen level needed for flame spread, making partial gravity potentially more hazardous than both Earth and microgravity (NTRS 20260000646)

## How confident we can be
- Confidence for thin fabric is high (evidence coverage 0.986) because 8 nearby runs exist; however, almost all solid runs are "sustained" (131 of 134), so a flammability limit cannot be located [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99]
- Confidence for thin solid is maximal (coverage 1.0) but limited by the same lack of non-burning solid data (131 of 134 sustained) [PSI-25] [PSI-99]
- Droplet data have full coverage (evidence coverage 1) and 100 % sustained runs, giving strong confidence for methanol and n-heptane under the tested conditions [PSI-69]
- Fire-resistant material data are sparse (8 runs total) and mixed; confidence is low and material-specific limits are unknown [PSI-25] [PSI-99]

## Gaps
- No microgravity test runs for thin fabric at oxygen levels below 20 % or pressures outside 101 kPa; flammability limit remains unbounded.
- Solid data lack sufficient extinction or no-ignition runs to define a quantitative flammability limit for any solid class.
- No PSI data for fire-resistant materials at oxygen > 22.2 % or under varied flow conditions; predictor provides no estimate.
- Partial-gravity (lunar, Martian) combustion has no test coverage; behavior may differ from both Earth-gravity and microgravity.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin-fabric burning at lower O₂ (≈ 15-18 %) and varied flow speeds to locate a flammability limit.
- Additional solid runs (both thin and thick) that intentionally achieve extinction or no-ignition to bound limits.
- Fire-resistant material tests across a broader O₂ range (up to 30 %) and with different ventilation rates to assess material-specific limits.
- Combustion experiments in partial-gravity environments (e.g., lunar-gravity simulators) to evaluate the hazard potential highlighted by NASA FM2 findings.
- Droplet combustion of additional fuels (e.g., ethanol) at 1 g and microgravity to compare physics estimates with measured limits.
